New folder

Folders can sit inside other folders. Deleting a folder keeps everything in it — the contents move up one level.
New section

A notebook is made of sections, and a section is made of pages. Deleting a section keeps its pages — they move to the unfiled group at the top.

Settings

Simple is the short list. All is every setting. Tap a row below for more in the guide.

While writing

Straightens lines and turns rough circles, boxes and triangles into clean ones. “Always” is the Samsung Notes way; it can catch a stray letter, and undo puts it straight back.

Each double-tap adds half a new page of paper. Writing near the bottom no longer grows the page on its own — that used to make the jump from one page to the next jerk.

Pen and eraser

On: the line stays the size you picked. Off: pressing harder makes a thicker line. If the pen reports no pressure, speed is used instead — unless this box is ticked.

If the eraser seems to miss your writing, make it bigger. “Wipe an area” in the ink bar uses roughly double this.

On: holding erases only while the nib stays down, so there is no eraser mode to get stuck in. Off: the hold turns the eraser on and leaves it on until you hold again.

Press the side button to turn the eraser on. Press it again to get the last pen back. It does not matter whether the nib is on the glass or hovering. You do not have to hold the button and then touch. If the button never reacts, turn Air Actions off (Settings → Advanced features → S Pen) so Chrome can see it.

While the pen is present, a finger neither draws nor scrolls.

How my handwriting looks

Steadies the wobble in a stroke. Higher is neater but rounder; 0 leaves your writing exactly as drawn. Applies to new strokes only, so nothing already written is changed.

Rounds the joins between the points the pen reported. The line still passes through every one of them, so this softens the joins without reshaping your letters. It changes only how the ink is drawn, not what is stored, so it improves writing you have already done — and 0 gives you plain straight joins back.

The line trails the nib slightly, so a tremor never reaches the page at all. Unlike the two above, this works while you write rather than tidying up afterwards, and it keeps corners sharp. High values feel like writing through treacle — 20 to 40 is usually enough.

Which to use. Try Steady my hand first; it is the one that changes how writing feels. Curve tidies what is already on the page. Smoothing is the strongest and the most likely to round off small letters.

Scrolling and zoom

Applies to one finger and to two fingers alike, so scrolling feels the same whether the zoom is locked or not. Set the first to 0 for no glide at all.

The zoom buttons and the two-finger pinch both stop at these.

The shortcuts bar

A small bar you can drag and shrink. It has Home (open another notebook without closing this one), Open (the notebooks you already have open), and Places (this notebook’s sections and bookmarked pages).

The favourites bar

Use the arrows below to put the tools in the order you want them down the bar.

Tick what it should carry. Tapping a tool you are already holding opens its colour and thickness beside the bar.

Bars and screen

Immerse hides every bar at once; a single button brings them back. “Show the tools” brings them back with typing and pen folded, so you start on the small note bar.

Untick anything you never use and it leaves the bar.

The page
Backups and menus

Shown once when you open the app, with Save backup and Later.

Off until you paste the password (the server address can stay as it is). They stay on this device only — never in the public app. Notes, handwriting and structure copy across. Class recordings stay on the device that made them. A Sync button appears at the top once it is on.

Sync is off.

What is in Simple

These choices only apply when Simple is on. All still shows everything.

Untick a button and it leaves the short toolbars. The All view still has it.

Data

Use Save notes every day. It keeps your writing, handwriting and pictures, and leaves class recordings out so the file stays small enough to save even when you have many hours of audio. Recordings stay on this device. Save everything including recordings is only for a small library — a big audio library can make that one fail.

Keep both never loses writing: where a page was edited on both devices, yours stays exactly as it is and the other device's copy arrives beside it, marked “from…” and sitting next to its twin in the page order so it is easy to compare the two and merge them by hand. The other three settings pick one copy and discard the other. Opening a notes-only file never throws away recordings already on this device.

To copy notes to the computer automatically, open Settings → Backups and menus, paste the server address and password, then Save and test. Sync stays off until you do that.
